chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh ibn Thabit from 'Amr ibn Jumay' from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no riba (usury/interest) between a man and his son, and there is no riba between a master and his slave.'
ai.seo_question: Is interest (riba) applicable between a father and son?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that riba (usury) is not applicable in transactions between a father and his son, or between a master and his slave, distinguishing these relationships from general commercial debt. It highlights the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence regarding familial and hierarchical bonds, where the strict prohibitions of riba are relaxed to facilitate intra-family financial support. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for understanding the nuances of debt and gift in close kinship ties.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashaab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Muaz Bin Sabit, from Amro Bin Jumie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no interest (usury) in between the man and his son, and there is no interest (usury) in between the master and his slave’.
en.sarwar: 1. Hamid ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Khashshab from ibn Baqqah from Mu’adh ibn Thabit from ‘Amr ibn Jumay‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘There is no Riba ’ between a man and his sons as well between a master and his slave.”’
